name: dpa4
summary: Skill for finetuning and deploying the DPA4 (DeepMD) machine-learning force field using deepmd-kit 3.1.2. It covers the dp workflow: converting datasets to HDF5, generating the version-matched input.json, finetuning from a pre-trained checkpoint, freezing to .pt2, and evaluating on datasets. It also explains how to use the frozen .pt2 model in ASE (e.g. NEB calculations) and LAMMPS via pair_style deepmd, including the required `atom_modify map yes` and multi-GPU MPI launch. Input/output file formats (*.hdf5, *.json, *.pt, *.pt2, lcurve.out, *.out) are documented. A quick formula relates n_structures and mean_natoms to training_natoms so that epochs contain 50-75 steps.

references.purpose: Template for job submission, intended only for StepNode.

scripts.purpose: Convert an extxyz structure file into HDF5 dataset format required by dp (usage: python3 extxyz_to_hdf5.py <path_to_extxyz> <path_to_hdf5>).
Generate the input.json file for dp finetuning/training, taking training data paths and training_natoms etc.; only compatible with checkpoint version DPA4-Neo-OMat24-v20260805.pt.
Print the mean number of atoms per structure and the total number of structures in an HDF5 dataset, used to pick an appropriate training_natoms (usage: python3 mean_natoms.py --hdf5 data.hdf5).

name: mlff-active-learning
summary: This skill describes how to obtain a high-precision machine learning force field (MLFF) via finetuning and active learning, primarily targeting catalysis computations with DPA/DeepMD. The core loop is sampling & DFT labelling, finetuning the MLFF, then MLFF-driven relaxation/NEB or MD, repeating until trajectories converge within reasonable step counts (no more structures extractable). It details a catalysis workflow (build initial dataset by rattling IS/FS and NEB paths, finetune DPA4, run relaxation/NEB, check trajectories, iterate) and a simpler general-system workflow for MD/EOS studies. It also advises separate finetuning per system (by element composition/chemistry) and provides file/state management guidance using step directories plus report.md and state.md. Iterating always refinetunes from scratch so all datasets share equal epoch coverage.

scripts.purpose: Inspect a relaxation/NEB/MD trajectory; if it is problematic (too long or unconverged), extract structures from it (with options like -n number of structures, --neb to ignore fixed IS/FS endpoints, --nstep_thres threshold) for subsequent DFT labelling.
Collect the computed (DFT single-point) structures into a single extxyz file to form the training dataset.
Perturb (rattle) atomic positions and optionally the cell (-c) of input structures to enlarge the configuration space covered by the training dataset.

Run structure relaxation (fixed cell, with optional bond-length constraint and adsorbate-index checks) or NEB using an ASE/DPA force field, producing result structures plus a state .json and .traj files to record convergence status.
Run structure relaxation (relaxable cell) and NPT molecular dynamics with a DPA MLFF at specified temperature/pressure, timestep, and step counts for sampling.
Sort the elements of a POSCAR file (needed after e.g. ase .repeat() which does not preserve element ordering).

name: stepnode-tools
summary: StepNode tools are organized into tool collections accessed via `get_tool_collection_infos` and `load_tool_collection`. The `structure_building_tools` collection builds initial/final states, adsorption structures, and initial NEB paths on surfaces. The `reaction_system_tools` collection generates, edits, and visualizes reaction networks, with several Human-In-The-Loop (HITL) tools that pause the agent to collect arguments. The workflow involves creating a reaction system, generating elementary steps, iteratively editing (deleting species/reactions, merging reactions) with user inspection via rendered PNGs, then dumping, binding to a surface, and deleting the system. No standalone scripts or reference files accompany this skill.

name: structure-building
summary: This skill demonstrates building simple structures with ase and pymatgen, noting that these libraries only cover simple/standard cases and complex cases should use specialized tools or user-provided structures. It covers format conversion between structure file types (e.g., OUTCAR to extxyz via ase, POSCAR to cif via pymatgen). It shows building molecules from chemical formula, SMILES string, or molecular graph, and building simple bulk crystals with ase.build.bulk. It also covers building slabs/surfaces by ase (fcc100/110/111/211, bcc100/110/111, hcp0001, hcp10m10) or by pymatgen for complex slabs, warning that pymatgen tends to build tilted slabs so ase is preferred for simple fcc/hcp/bcc cases. Three wrapper scripts are provided in the scripts dir.

scripts.purpose: Builds a molecule from a chemical formula, a SMILES string, or a molecular graph (with --vertexes and --edges).

Builds a slab/surface, either a simple one via ase (-e element, -f facet, -s size, -v vacuum, --nfix) or a complex one from a bulk structure via pymatgen (--bulk, --miller, --size_ab, --size_c, --size_fix).
Converts between a conventional cell and a primitive cell (--conv to go to primitive, --prim to go to conventional).

name: ts-search
summary: This skill provides instructions for locating transition states (TS) on the potential energy surface using VASP (compiled with VTST) and ASE. It covers two main approaches: PES interpolation via NEB (building and relaxing an initial minimum energy path between initial and final states, using scripts like neb_make.py, with detailed VASP INCAR tags and optimizer choices such as IOPT=7/FIRE, IOPT=1/LBFGS, IBRION=1/RMM-DIIS, plus ASE/MLFF workflows), and PES walking via Dimer (which requires a TS guess and MODECAR typically generated from NEB results with neb2dim.py). It also describes practical wisdom such as system complexity assessment, re-interpolation of distorted paths, and frequency analysis to compute vibration free energy and validate the TS. Related scripts handle NEB path generation, force/energy reporting, slab atom fixing, vibration mode extraction, and structure distance calculation.

references.purpose: File template for job submission, only for StepNode

scripts.purpose: Calculate the distance between two structures
Fix the slab atoms for frequency analysis, using --relax_ind to specify which atoms are allowed to relax
Calculate vibration free energy from the OUTCAR of a frequency analysis, with temperature (-t) and isotope options
Print the wavenumbers of vibration modes and extract a specific vibration mode into a mode_i file (usable as MODECAR for Dimer)
Convert the results of an NEB calculation to the inputs of a Dimer calculation
Print the max force, DFT energy and relative energy of NEB images
Interpolate between relaxed IS and FS structures to generate an initial NEB path (with nimages or spacing options)

name: vasp
summary: Provides general knowledge of VASP usage, focusing on the four basic input files (INCAR, POSCAR, KPOINTS, POTCAR) and practical calculation guidance. Covers INCAR settings for precision, electronic algorithm (ALGO), geometry optimization (IBRION/ISIF/POTIM), smearing (ISMEAR/SIGMA), and advanced options (ISPIN, LDAU, IVDW) that require user confirmation. Explains KPOINTS construction rules (inverse proportion to lattice length, gamma-only for molecules, KSPACING for bulk) and POTCAR selection/assembly via scripts. Includes practical tips: minimize INCAR tags, pause for user review, keep LWAVE/LCHARG false, maintain consistent tags, and use staged low-precision calculations to reach convergence.

references.purpose: File template for job submission, usable only for StepNode.

scripts.purpose: Generate a KPOINTS file for normal or band structure calculations.
Print recommended POTCAR names for given elements (e.g. via -e option).
